title: Hydrothermal synthesis of different structures TiO2 and photocatalytic activity for tetracycline and Cr (VI) removal
content:
Abstract

Ensuring the removal of pollutants including organic and heavy metal contaminants through cost-effective methods was crucial for mitigating toxicity risks. In this study, a facile hydrothermal method was employed to synthesize TiO2, encompassing flower-like TiO2, TiO2 nanorods and TiO2 nanosheets. And the photocatalytic activities were analysed for removing tetracycline (TC) and Cr (VI) in solution. The photocatalytic activity revealed that TiO2 nanosheets exhibited the highest performance, followed by TiO2 nanorods, flower-like TiO2, and finally, P25, which hierarchy was attributed to differences in band structure and the enhanced utilization of light. Furthermore, alterations in the TiO2 structures were found to be effective in promoting the efficient separation of electron–hole pairs and suppressing their recombination. And the generated h + and/or •O2 − were the predominant reactive species for removal of TC and Cr (VI). Collectively, this work provided a valuable blueprint for enhancing the applicability of TiO2 in environmental remediation and energy-related photocatalytic processes.
